results.content:
(Credit: Nomad/PCMag)

In the US, Nomad offers six regular plans: 1GB for $4.50 (seven days), 1GB for $6 (seven days), 3GB for $11 (30 days), 5GB for $14 (30 days), 10GB for $24 (30 days), and 20GB for $35 (30 days). Though they offer the same 1GB of data, the $4.50 and $6.00 plans are indeed different. The $4.50 plan supports AT&T and T-Mobile and starts automatically when connected to a network or after a 30-day window. The $6.00 plan is limited to just AT&T but provides a more flexible 60-day activation window.

Nomad also offers shorter day plans ranging from 1 to 10 days that come with 1GB of high-speed data per day plus unlimited data throttled to 512Kbps. The website and app clearly outline each plan’s details, and all listed prices include applicable taxes.

(Credit: Nomad/PCMag) [...] (Credit: Nomad/PCMag)

Nomad's US pricing is in line with other data-only service providers like Airalo and Saily, which charge $4.50 and $4.39, respectively, for 1GB of data over 7 days.

To use Nomad's eSIM service, your device needs to be unlocked and eSIM compatible. Many modern phones, such as the Apple iPhone 16 and the Samsung Galaxy S24, support eSIMs. If you are unsure if your device will work with Nomad, the company lists the phones, tablets, and laptops that are compatible with its service. [...] (Credit: Iyaz Akhtar)

You can view your data usage in the Manage tab of the Nomad app, where you can also see details like when your plan will expire and buy more data. If your data is running low or is set to expire, you will receive a notification. You can purchase additional data at the same price as regular plans. For example, an additional 1GB costs $4.50.

I’ve tried several eSIM providers so far, but the most recent one I tested was Ubigi. My package included 10 GB of data for 30 days, which is the most popular plan for that destination. The setup was simple, mobile data speed was excellent, and I didn’t experience any gaps in coverage while using it.

Here is some info about the Ubigi eSIM:

Ubigi eSIM is also quite reliable because it’s a part of a larger telecom company which is operating worldwide, meaning they use the existing infrastructure and are not a third party provider. [...] First, visit Ubigi website and search for your travel destination. Once you get there, you can see different financial plans. Purchase the eSIM data plan of your choice.

Next, downloaded the Ubigi app to your phone and create your account. Setting that up is super easy.

Upon purchase, you receive an email with a QR code. Scan it to install your eSIM on your device. You’ll need to click on the ‘sign-up button’ to connect eSIM to your account. And after that, you’re good to go. I recommend installing your eSIM before your trip. Upon arrival, make sure to turn on your Ubigi line in your phone settings. Then, you can start using your mobile data, track how much you have spent and easily top it up. [...] Getting a prepaid eSIM means there are no hidden costs, and you won’t receive a huge bill once back from your holidays (something I was always dreadful would happen).

The eSIM options are much cheaper than using the data on roaming provided by your mobile provider, as well. And they are especially useful if you’ll visit multiple destinations during your trip because you don’t need to get a physical sim card in each new country you visit.

Holafly eSIM cards are one of the options offering unlimited data plans, so there’s no need to restrict how many videos and photos you send back to friends and family at home. It is more expensive than the others but you don’t have to keep topping up as most of its plans offer unlimited data. Holafly covers 160+ destinations and has long-term plans of up to 90 days. 5.Maya US$6.00/3GB [...] 5.Maya US$6.00/3GB

US-based Maya operates in 194 countries. While they also offer unlimited data plan options, they do not provide global plans like some competitors. However, you can use Maya eSIMs for hotspotting, giving you more flexibility when traveling and needing to connect multiple devices.

eSIMs offer numerous advantages for modern travelers and are definitely a useful travel essential. With the ability to switch between carriers without the need for a physical SIM card, users can easily access local data plans and avoid exorbitant roaming fees. Opt for an unlimited plan if you think you’ll need a lot of data. Otherwise, go for a standard plan with a fixed data limit.

## 4. Regional eSIM Price Comparison

 Europe: 5GB ($5–$15) | 10GB ($10–$25) — excellent multi-country bundles, lowest average cost due to roaming agreements.
 Asia: 5GB ($3–$20) — Southeast Asia offers the world's cheapest data; Japan and Korea are mid-to-high tier with premium networks.
 USA & Canada: 5GB ($10–$25) | 10GB ($20–$40) — highest regional cost due to carrier infrastructure.
 Global plans (multi-country): 5GB ($15–$30) | 10GB ($25–$50) — convenience for multi-region trips, higher cost per GB.

## 5. Provider-by-Provider Price Comparison [...] ## 7. How to Compare eSIM Prices Correctly

 Always calculate cost per GB (total price ÷ data amount).
 Compare validity vs data ratio: a longer plan often yields lower daily cost.
 Check network coverage quality: 4G/5G access, local carrier partners, fair usage policy (FUP).
 Hotspot/tethering rules — essential for laptop sharing and multi-device usage.
 Compare at least 2–3 providers (Airalo, Nomad, Holafly, ByteSIM) before purchasing.
